newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Compart sees better 96 second half.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Compart sees better 96 second half.

text.p: Italian financial holding group Compart expects to see improved results in the second half of 1996, managing director Enrico Bondi said.
"There is a more positive view than in the first half and in the first six months of 1995," Bondi told a shareholders meeting.

Compart, formerly known as Ferruzzi Finanziaria, posted first half 1996 consolidated net profit of 186 billion lire against 287 billion lire in the first half of 1995 which included 272 billion lire of capital gains due to the transfer of its Montedison company's plastics activities to Montell.

Bondi said he expected Compart to break even at parent level. In the first half of 1996, Compart parent company pretax profit was 70 billion lire against a 128 billion lire loss in the same 1995 period.
Compart said this was the first time since 1991 it had shown a profit at the parent level.
Bondi said Montedison "has a clearly more positive trend" whereas its Calcestruzzi unit had suffered in the first half "and is still suffering" apart from its cement sector which "is doing well".
He said insurer La Fondiaria had every reason to end the year with positive results after first half parent pre-tax profit of 68.6 billion lire against 28.8 billion. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
